launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | Zuma
launches.mission_desc: Unknown payload built by Northrop Grumman for an undisclosed customer, most likely a government organisation.

launches.name: Long March 2D | SuperView-1 (Gaojing 1-03 & Gaojing 1-04)
launches.mission_desc: These two satellites, also known as SuperView-2 constellation, are remote sensing satellites to operate in a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit. This is a second pair of such satellites to be launched for the SuperView company. They are capable of providing imagery with 0.5 m panchromatic resolution and 2 m multispectral resolution.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity GF07
launches.mission_desc: Free glide test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M7 & M8
launches.mission_desc: The BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) is a Chinese satellite navigation system. It consists of two separate satellite constellations â€“ a limited test system that has been operating since 2000, and a full-scale global navigation system that is currently under construction. Beidou-3 are the third generation of navigation satellites which are launched into medium Earth orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: PSLV XL | Cartosat-2F (Cartosat-2S4)
launches.mission_desc: Cartosat-2F is eighth of Cartosat series of Earth observation satellites to be deployed in a sun-synchronous orbit. Its main purpose is to collect high resolution large-scale maps which will be used for urban planning, infrastructure development, utilities planning and traffic management.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Delta IV M+(5,2) | NROL-47
launches.mission_desc: Classified payload for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office.

launches.name: Long March 2D | LKW-3 (Land Survey Satellite-3)
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Epsilon | ASNARO-2
launches.mission_desc: ASNARO-2 (Advanced Satellite with New system ARchitecture for Observation) is an advanced small X-band radar satellite for Earth observation for Japan. Satellite weighs about 495 kg and is to operate in sun-synchronous orbit.

launches.name: Long March 11 | Jilin-1-07 (Deqing-1), Jilin-1-08
launches.mission_desc: Jilin-1 is a series of Chinese commercial remote sensing satellites. These two satellites are sharing the ride with several cubesats.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Atlas V 411 | SBIRS GEO Flight 4 (SBIRS GEO-3)
launches.mission_desc: This geostationary satellite is tasked with providing capabilities for early missile warning and missile defense.

launches.name: Electron | Still Testing
launches.mission_desc: The second test flight of the Electron small satellite launch vehicle. It is also the first Electron flight to carry commercial payload. It includes a Dove cubesat for company Planet intended for  Earth observation. And also two Lemur-2 cubesats for company Spire which carry payloads for meteorology and ship traffic tracking.
launches.location: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, Mahia Peninsula, New Zealand

launches.name: Long March 2C | 3 x Yaogan-30
launches.mission_desc: Yaogan is a series of Chinese reconnaissance satellites.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | Al Yah 3 & SES-14
launches.mission_desc: Al Yah 3 is a geostationary communications satellite built by Orbital ATK for Yahsat. It weighs 3790 kg, carries 53 Ka-band user beams and 4 gateway beams, and is intended for 15 years of operation in orbit. Al Yah 3 will provide telecommunication services to Africa and Brazil. SES-14 is also a communications satellite to be placed in geostationary orbit, replacing NSS-806 satellite. SES-14 coverage includes the Americas and the North Atlantic Region. Spacecraft also carries a hosted payload for NASA, Global-Scale Observations of the Limb and Disk (GOLD) mission, which will be imaging Earth's thermosphere and ionospehere for two years.
launches.fail_reason: Payloads placed into an incorrect orbit.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | GovSat (SES-16)
launches.mission_desc: GovSat, also known as SES-16 is a communications satellite for LuxGovSat S.A., which is a public-private joint venture between the Luxembourg government and SES. Staying in 21.5Â° East orbital position, it is intended to operate for 15 years, using X-band and military Ka-band frequencies to support multiple missions.

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1a/Fregat-M | Kanopus-V No.3 & Kanopus-V No.4
launches.mission_desc: Kanopus-V is a series of small remote sensing satellites, dedicated to monitoring manmade and natural emergencies, detecting forest fires and major emissions of atmosphere pollutants. Its other uses are monitoring of agriculture, water and coastal resoures, land use. Each satellite weighs about 500 kg and is placed into sun-synchronous orbit, where it is planned to operate for about 5 years.

launches.name: Long March 2D | Zhangheng-1 (CSES)
launches.mission_desc: Zhangheng-1, also known as CSES (China Seismo-Electromagnetic Satellite) is a scientific mission dedicated to studying the ionospheric precursors of earthquakes.  Data collected by the mission will also allow studying solar-terrestrial interactions and phenomena of solar physics. This mission is a collaboration between China National Space Administration and the Italian Space Agency. CSES satellite weighs about 730 kg and it is to reside in a 98Â° sun-synchronous circular orbit at an altitude about 500 km, where it is expected to operate for 5 years.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: SS-520-5 | TRICOM-1R
launches.mission_desc:
TRICOM-1 is an experimental 3U cubsat build by University of Tokyo. It is equipped with 5 small cameras for Earth imaging purposes, and is also tasked with storing and transmitting data between ground terminals.
TRICOM-1R is a replacement for the failed SS-520-4 launch of TRICOM-1.

launches.name: Falcon Heavy | Demo (Test Flight)
launches.mission_desc: This will be the inaugural flight of the Falcon Heavy. The test payload will be SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's midnight cherry Tesla Roadster playing Space Oddity. Destination: An elliptical, heliocentric orbit. Apoapsis: Around Mars' orbital distance.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M3 & M4
launches.mission_desc: The BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) is a Chinese satellite navigation system. It consists of two separate satellite constellations â€“ a limited test system that has been operating since 2000, and a full-scale global navigation system that is currently under construction. Beidou-3 are the third generation navigation satellites which are launched into medium Earth orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1a | Progress MS-08 (69P)
launches.mission_desc: The Progress resupply vehicle is an automated, unpiloted version of the Soyuz spacecraft that is used to bring supplies and fuel to the International Space Station.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | PAZ & Microsat-2a, Microsat-2b
launches.mission_desc: PAZ is a military Earth radar observation satellite, designed and built by Airbus Defence and Space for Spain. The satellite is owned and operated by Hisdesat. The PAZ satellite is equipped with an advanced radar instrument designed for high flexibility, and the capability to operate in numerous modes allowing for the choice of several different image configurations. It will be able to generate images with up to 25 cm resolution. Designed for a mission of five and a half years, PAZ will orbit Earth 15 times per day, covering an area of over 300,000 square kilometres. On its slightly inclined quasi-polar orbit, PAZ will cover the entire globe in 24 hours, serving both government and commercial needs. Satellite is sharing the ride with two small SpaceX satellites. These will test the technologies for the planned satellite network called Starlink, which will consist of roughly 4000 satellites providing space-based Internet around the globe.

launches.name: H-IIA 202 | IGS Optical 6
launches.mission_desc: Information Gathering Satellite (IGS) is a Japanese governmental spy satellite program. IGS Optical 6, as the name suggests, is an optical reconnaissance satellite.

launches.name: Atlas V 541 | GOES-S
launches.mission_desc: The Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite-S Series (GOES-S) is the second of the next generation of geostationary weather satellites. The four satellites of the series will provide advanced imaging with increased spatial resolution and faster coverage for more accurate forecasts, real-time mapping of lightning activity, and improved monitoring of solar activity. GOES-S  will provide continuous imagery and atmospheric measurements of the Western Hemisphere. GOES-S will be the primary tool for the detection and tracking of hurricanes and severe weather. Once operational as GOES-17, the satellite wil replace GOES-15 satellite.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | Hispasat 30W-6 (Hispasat 1F)
launches.mission_desc: Hispasat 30W-6, also known as Hispasat 1F, is a Spanish geostationary communications satellite. Joining the Hispasat fleet, this satellite is to operate in orbit for 15 years, providing services to Europe, North Africa, North America and South America. It  is a replacement for the Hispasat 1D satellite at 30Âº West longtitude in geostationary orbit. Satellite launch mass is about 6000 kg and it is equipped with Ku-, Ka- and C-band transponders.

launches.name: Soyuz STB/Fregat | O3b FM13-16
launches.mission_desc: The O3b Satellite Constellation is a satellite constellation designed for telecommunications and data backhaul from remote locations.

launches.name: Long March 2D | LKW-4 (Land Survey Satellite-4)
launches.mission_desc: Land Survey Satellite-4 is the fourth in a series of Chinese remote sensing satellites.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-08
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-08 begins expedition 55 by carrying Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Artemyev, NASA astronauts Andrew Feustel and Richard Arnold to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: GSLV Mk II | GSAT-6A
launches.mission_desc: GSAT-6A is and Indian geostationary communications satellite for multi-media mobile applications. Weighing about 2000 kg, satellite is expected to operate in orbit for 9 years.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre Second Launch Pad

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1v | VNIIEM EMKA (Kosmos 2525)
launches.mission_desc: The payload for the Soyuz-2-1v launch is a small reconnaissance satellite developed by VNIIEM and known by the acronym EMKA ("Experimental Small Space Apparatus"). Launch was originally scheduled for October and then slipped to November, December and eventually January due to technical problems with the payload.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M9 & M10
launches.mission_desc: The BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) is a Chinese satellite navigation system. It consists of two separate satellite constellations â€“ a limited test system that has been operating since 2000, and a full-scale global navigation system that is currently under construction. Beidou-3 are the third generation of navigation satellites which are launched into medium Earth orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | Iridium-5
launches.mission_desc: SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and data satellite communications. This is the fifth set of 10 satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will launch for Iridiumâ€™s next generation global satellite constellation, IridiumÂ® NEXT.

launches.name: Long March 4C | Gaofen 1-02, 1-03 & 1-04
launches.mission_desc: Gaofen is a series of Chinese civilian Earth observation satellites. These three satellites are to be operated together with the Gaofen-1 satellite, which was launched in 2013.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | SpX CRS-14
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their 14th operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity PF01
launches.mission_desc: First powered test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | DSN 1 & HYLAS 4
launches.mission_desc: DSN-1 (also known as Kirameki 1, Superbird 8 or Superbird B3) is Japanese X-band military communications satellite. It was planned to be launched in 2016, however the satellite was damaged during transport to the launch site and repairs delayed the launch. The satellite is to replace aging Superbird-B2 satellite at 162Â° East in geostationary orbit. HYLAS 4 is a communications satellite build by Orbital ATK for Avanti Communication. It features hybrid propulsion system, with traditional chemical thrusters for orbit raising and ion engines for stationkeeping. The satellite carries 66 high-throughput Ka-band beams and will provide services to regions of Africa and Europe.

launches.name: Long March 4C | 3 x Yaogan-31-01
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: PSLV XL | IRNSS-1I
launches.mission_desc: This is a replacement satellite for the IRNSS-1H of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System. The constellation will provide India with an alternative to GPS and will be used for military and civilian use. Located at a geosynchronous orbit, the system will be operated by the Indian government.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Atlas V 551 | AFSPC-11
launches.mission_desc: Primary payload of the mission is the Continuous Broadcast Augmenting SATCOM (CBAS) satellite, which will be placed in geosynchronous orbit. It will continously relay data from from existing military communications satellites to support senior leaders and combatant commanders. This mission will also launch a number of secondary payloads hosted on the ESPA Augmented Geostationary Laboratory Experiment (EAGLE).

launches.name: Proton-M/Briz-M | Blagovest No.12L (Kosmos 2526)
launches.mission_desc: The second of four planned Blagovest communication satellites. It is a high throughput communications satellite used for high speed internet services, TV, radio broadcasting and voice/video networking.
launches.lsp: Khrunichev State Research and Production Space Center

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite)
launches.mission_desc: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) is a NASA space telescope, designed to search for exoplanets using the transit method. TESS will identify planets ranging from Earth-sized to gas giants, orbiting a wide range of stellar types and orbital distances. The principal goal of the TESS mission is to detect small planets with bright host stars in the solar neighborhood, so that detailed characterizations of the planets and their atmospheres can be performed.

launches.name: Rokot / Briz-KM | Sentinel-3B
launches.mission_desc: Sentinel-3B is the second in a constellation of earth observation satellites developed by ESA to provide near real time data for the Global Monitoring for Environment and Security Program. Sentinel-3B contains a temperature scanner, colour instrument and altimeter for monitoring the sea and land. The satellite focuses on providing accurate data about the oceans and in addition also provides information about wildfires and vegetation.

launches.name: Long March 11 | Zhuhai-1-02
launches.mission_desc: Multiple satellite mission consisting of five Earth-imaging satellites, which comprise the second group of commercial imaging satellites for Zhuhai Orbita Control Engineering Ltd.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: New Shepard | NS-8
launches.mission_desc: NS-8 is Blue Origin's second commercial flight. It carried payloads from various customers on a sub-orbital launch for 3 minutes of microgravity.
launches.pad: West Texas Suborbital Launch Site/ Corn Ranch
launches.location: Corn Ranch, Van Horn, TX, USA

launches.name: Long March 3B/E | APStar-6C
launches.mission_desc: APStar-6C is a commercial communications satellite for APT Satellite Company Ltd under an end-to-end contract signed with China Great Wall Industry Corp. (CGWIC) for satellite production and launch services. It will deliver VSAT, video distribution, Direct-to-home television and cellular backhaul to the Asia-Pacific Region.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Atlas V 401 | InSight, Mars Cube One 1 & Mars Cube One 2
launches.mission: InSight, Mars Cube One 1 & Mars Cube One 2
launches.mission_desc: InSight is a robotic Mars lander designed to study the interior and subsurface of Mars, which would in turn help scientists to understand the Earth and Solar System history. Two 6U CubeSats will piggyback with the InSight mission to help relay communications during the probe's entry, descent, and landing (EDL) phase.

launches.name: Long March 4C | Gaofen 5
launches.mission_desc:
Gaofen is a series of civilian Earth observation satellites developed and launched for the China High-definition Earth Observation System (CHEOS), a state-sponsored programme aimed to develop a near-real time, all-weather, global surveillance network consisting of satellite, near-space (stratosphere) airships, and aerial observation platforms.
Based on the SAST5000B bus, Gaofen 5 will carry six types of payloads, including visible and short-wave infra hyper-spectral camera, spectral imager, greenhouse gas detector, atmospheric environment infrared detector at very high spectral resolution, differential absorption spectrometer for atmospheric trace gas, and multi-angle polarization detector. The satellite has a designed life of 8 years. It is to be launched atop of a Long March 4C to a 705km Sun Syncronous Orbit (SSO).
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Bangabandhu-1
launches.mission_desc: The Bangabandhu 1 (BD-1) satellite, the first geostationary communications satellite of Bangladesh. Satellite is to be located at 119.1Â° East longitude slot in geostationary orbit, where it will provide service to Bangladesh and neighbouring countries. Satellite is build by Thales Aleinia Space. It is based on Spacebus 4000B2 platform, weighs 3500 kg and is fitted with Ku-Band and C-Band transponders. The major applications of the spacecraft include DTH, very small aperture terminal communications, backhaul and trunking, network restoration, and disaster preparedness and relief.

launches.name: Long March 4C | Queqiao (Chang'e 4 relay satellite)
launches.mission_desc: Chang'e 4 is a Chinese lunar exploration mission that will incorporate an orbiter, a robotic lander and rover. The orbiter serves as a communications relay satellite. It will be placed into a halo orbit around the Earth-Moon L2 Lagrange point and is planned to support further missions to the far side of the Moon.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Antares 230 | Cygnus CRS OA-9 (S.S. J.R. Thompson)
launches.mission_desc: This is the tenth planned flight of the Orbital ATK's unmanned resupply spacecraft Cygnus and its ninth flight to the International Space Station under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | Iridium-6 & GRACE-FO
launches.mission_desc:
SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and data satellite communications. This is the sixth set of 10 satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will launch for Iridiumâ€™s next generation global satellite constellation, IridiumÂ® NEXT.
Sharing this launch is the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-on mission, which is a joint project of NASA and the German Research Centre for Geosciences. It's goal is to track Earth's water movement to monitor changes in underground water storage, the amount of water in large lakes and rivers, soil moisture, ice sheets and glaciers, and sea level caused by the addition of water to the ocean.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity PF02
launches.mission_desc: Powered test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Long March 2D | Gaofen 6 & Luojia-1
launches.mission_desc: Gaofen is a series of civilian Earth observation satellites developed and launched for the China High-definition Earth Observation System (CHEOS), a state-sponsored programme aimed to develop a near-real time, all-weather, global surveillance network consisting of satellite, near-space (stratosphere) airships, and aerial observation platforms. Luojia-1 is a 6U Earth observation cubesat prototype.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | SES-12
launches.mission_desc: SES-12 is a geostationary communications satellite. It is to provide direct-to-home broadcasting, high throughput satellite data connectivity and other telecommunication servies to Middle East and the Asia-Pacific region. It is a replacement for the NSS-6 satellite and is expected to operate for 15 years.

launches.name: Long March 3A | Fengyun-2H
launches.mission_desc: Fengyun is China's meteorogical satellite program. It includes polar-orbiting and geostationary spacecrafts. Fengyun-2H is a geostationary satellite expected to operate in orbit for about 5 years.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-09
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-09 begins expedition 56 by carrying Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Prokopyev, ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst and NASA astronaut Serena AuÃ±Ã³n-Chancellor to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: H-IIA 202 | IGS Radar 6
launches.mission_desc: IGS Radar is a family of Japanese radar reconnaissance satellites that serve both Japan's national defense and civil natural disaster monitoring. IGS Radar 5 is the fifth generation of satellites. Equipped with synthetic aperture radar, it is able to image targets even in darkness and bad weather.

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1b/Fregat-M | Glonass-M No. 56 (Kosmos 2527)
launches.mission_desc: GLONASS is a global satellite navigation system similar to the American GPS system.

launches.name: Long March 2C | XJS-A & XJS-B
launches.mission_desc: A pair of experimental satellites to conduct tests of intersatellite communication links and trial new Earth observation technology.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | SpX CRS-15
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their 15th operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Long March 2C/SMA | PRSS-1 & PakTes-1A
launches.mission_desc: The Pakistan Remote Sensing Satellite (PRSS) is a dual purpose Earh observation and optical satellite. It is to operate in sun-synchronous orbit with a planned lifetime of 5 years.  PakTes-1A is a remote sensing satellite built by Pakistan's space agency with assistance from Space Advisory Company of South Africa.

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1A | Progress MS-09 (70P)
launches.mission_desc: The Progress resupply vehicle is an automated, unpiloted version of the Soyuz spacecraft that is used to bring supplies and fuel to the International Space Station.

launches.name: New Shepard | NS-9
launches.mission_desc: The third commercial flight for Blue Origin. NS-9 carried various payloads on a sub-orbital flight. It also tested the capsule escape rockets at high altitude.
launches.pad: West Texas Suborbital Launch Site/ Corn Ranch
launches.location: Corn Ranch, Van Horn, TX, USA

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Telstar 19 VANTAGE
launches.mission_desc: Telstar 19 VANTAGE, or Telstar 19V, is a communications satellite built by Space Systems Loral for the canadian satellite operator Telesat. The satellite is to be placed into 63Â° West orbital slot, where it will provide coverage for North And South America.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ES | Galileo L10 (FOC FM19-FM22)
launches.mission_desc: The Galileo constellation is ESA's satellite navigation system and is expected to be completed by 2020. Galileo will provide Europe with an alternative to the American GPS and Russian GLONASS constellations, but will be interoperable with both systems.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Iridium-7
launches.mission_desc: SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and data satellite communications. This is the seventh set of 10 satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will launch for Iridiumâ€™s next generation global satellite constellation, IridiumÂ® NEXT.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity PF03
launches.mission_desc: Powered test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M5 & M6
launches.mission_desc: These two satellites will be used to provide global navigation coverage as part of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Long March 4B | Gaofen-11
launches.mission_desc: The Gaofen-11 satellite is believed to be a Earth-imaging satellite that Chinese state media claims, "can be used for land survey, urban planning, road network design, agriculture, and disaster relief".
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Merah Putih (Telkom-4)
launches.mission_desc: Telkom-4, also known as  Merah Putih, is an Indonesian geostationary communications satellite. It will replace the aging Telkom-1 satellite.

launches.name: Delta IV Heavy | Parker Solar Probe
launches.mission_desc:
Flying into the Sunâ€™s atmosphere (or corona) for the first time. Coming closer to the Sun than any previous spacecraft, Parker Solar Probe will employ a combination of in situ measurements and imaging to achieve the missionâ€™s primary
scientific goal: to understand how the Sunâ€™s corona is heated and how the solar wind is accelerated.

launches.name: Vega | ADM-Aeolus
launches.mission_desc: ADM-Aeolus was an Earth observation satellite built by Airbus Defense and Space for ESA. Its goal was to directly observe wind profiles from space on a global scale and provide data that could improve weather forecasting and advance understanding of atmospherics dynamics and climate. The Aeolus satellite weighed around 1366 kg and flew in a low sun-synchronous orbit at about 400 km altitude. It was desorbited and reentered the Earth's atmosphere on July 28, 2023 at approximately  19:00 UTC.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M11 & M12
launches.mission_desc: These two satellites will be used to provide global navigation coverage as part of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: SARGE | Launch 1 - "Pathfinder"
launches.mission_desc: First test launch of the SARGE reusable sounding rocket.

launches.name: Long March 2C | Haiyang 1C
launches.mission_desc: Haiyang is a series of Chinese marine remote sensing satellites. Haiyang 1C is the follow-up of the Haiyang 1A and 1B satellites. It is intended for ocean monitoring and will be providing data on the temperature and dynamics of coastal waters and global oceans in China.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Telstar 18 VANTAGE
launches.mission_desc: Telstar 18 VANTAGE, or Telstar 18V, is a communications satellite built by Space Systems Loral for the canadian satellite operator Telesat. The satellite is to provide coverage to the Asia Pacific region.

launches.name: Delta II 7420-10 | ICESat-2
launches.mission_desc: ICESat-2 (Ice, Cloud, and land Elevation Satellite 2) is a NASA Earth observation mission for measuring ice sheet elevation and sea ice freeboard, as well as land topography and vegetation characteristics.

launches.name: PSLV-CA | SSTL-S1 & NovaSAR-S
launches.mission_desc: The NovaSAR-S spacecraft carries a radar imaging instrument, and the mission was developed in partnership between the British government and the British satellite manufacturer SSTL. The SSTL-S1 satellite, also built by SSTL, is a high-resolution optical Earth observation satellite identical to three DMC3/TripleSat reconnaissance craft launched in 2015. Beijing-based 21AT will lease imaging capacity on the SSTL-S1 satellite. There are also several secondary payloads.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M13 & M14
launches.mission_desc: These two satellites will be used to provide global navigation coverage as part of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: H-IIB 304 | Kounotori 7 (HTV-7)
launches.mission_desc: Uncrewed cargo resupply mission to International Space Station.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | Azerspace-2/Intelsat-38 & Horizons 3e
launches.mission_desc: Azercosmos-2/Intelsat-38 is a geostationary telecommunications satellite. As the name suggests, satellite will be used jointly by Azercosmos and Intelsat. Horizons-3e, also known as IS-H3e, is a high throughput geostationary communications satellite ordered by Horizons Satellite, a joint venture of Intelsat and SKY Perfect JSAT Group. The spacecraft is designed and manufactured by Boeing on the Boeing-702MP platform.

launches.name: Kuaizhou 1A | Centispace-1-S1
launches.mission_desc: CentiSpace-1-S1 is an experimental satellite to test navigation and and positioning enhancement system being developed by Beijing Future Navigation Technology Co., Ltd.
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | SAOCOM 1A
launches.mission_desc: The SAOCOM 1A spacecraft is the first of the two SAOCOM constellation satellites. It is tasked with hydrology and land observaion, and will also operate jointly with the Italian COSMO-SkyMed constellation in X-band to provide frequent information relevant for emergency management.

launches.name: Long March 2C/YZ-1S | Yaogan-32-01
launches.mission_desc: Yaogan is a series of Chinese reconnaissance satellites.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-10
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-10 was expected to begin expedition 57 by carrying Roscosmos cosmonaut Alexey Ovchinin and NASA astronaut Nick Hague to the International Space Station. However a launch failure occurred resulting in a loss of vehicle during flight, both crew members returned to Earth nominally.
launches.fail_reason: An anomaly occurred during flight resulting in loss of vehicle, both crew members returned to Earth safely following a nominal ballistic abort.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M15 & M16
launches.mission_desc: These two satellites will be used to provide global navigation coverage as part of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Atlas V 551 | AEHF-4 (USA 288)
launches.mission_desc: This is the fourth satellite in the Advanced Extremely High Frequency (AEHF) system, which is a series of communications satellites operated by the United States Air Force Space Command. It provides global, survivable, protected communications capabilities for strategic command and tactical warfighters operating on ground, sea and air platforms.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | BepiColombo
launches.mission_desc: BepiColombo is a joint mission of the ESA and the JAXA to the planet Mercury. The mission comprises two satellites to be launched together: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO). The mission will perform a comprehensive study of Mercury, including its magnetic field, magnetosphere, interior structure and surface.

launches.name: Long March 4B | Haiyang 2B
launches.mission_desc: Haiyang is a series of Chinese marine remote sensing satellites. Haiyang 2B is a follow up to Haiyang 2A satellite. It is intended for monitoring the dynamic ocean environnement with microwave sensors to detect sea surface wind field, sea surface height and sea surface temperature.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1B | Lotos-S1 (Kosmos 2528)
launches.mission_desc: Lotos-S1 spacecraft is a part of the Liana constellation, designed for orbital electronic intelligence.

launches.name: Zhuque-1 | Weilai-1 (Future-1)
launches.mission_desc: The satellite is operated by China Central Television (CCTV) and is intended to carry out scientific expermients and perform Earth observation. Weilai-1 is expected to operate in sun-synchronous orbit for two years.
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China
launches.fail_reason: Attitude control failed after third stage ignition.

launches.name: Long March 2C | CFOSAT
launches.mission_desc: CFOSAT (China-France Oceanography SATellite) is a joint mission of the Chinese (CNSA) and French (CNES) space agencies with the goal to monitor the ocean surface winds and waves and to provide information on related ocean and atmospheric science and applications. The primary objective of CFOSAT is to monitor on a global scale the wind and waves at the ocean surface.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: H-IIA 202 | KhalifaSat & GOSAT-2
launches.mission_desc: KhalifaSat is an Earth observation satellite for UAE. KhalifaSat will provide high-resolution imagery of Earth to be used for various purposes, including urban planning, change monitoring, area classification, monitoring environmental change and aiding relief efforts for natural disasters. GOSAT 2 (Greenhouse gases Observing SATellite 2) is a Japanese satellite dedicated to greenhouse gas measurement from space. It's a follow on to the GOSAT mission and includes such improvements as an ability to gather more precise data and monitor carbon monoxide concentrations.

launches.name: Long March 3B | Beidou-3 G1
launches.mission_desc: This satellite is a part of the geostationary component of the 3rd phase of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system. It features a phased array antenna for navigation signals and a laser retroreflector and additionally deployable S/L-band and C-band antennas.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1b/Fregat-M | Glonass-M No. 57 (Kosmos 2529)
launches.mission_desc: Glonass-M, also known as Uragan-M, are the second generation of Uragan satellite design used for GLONASS satellite navigation system. GLONASS is a Russian space-based navigation system comparable to the similar GPS and Galileo systems. This generation improves on accuracy, power consumption and design life. Each satellite weighs 1415 kg, is equipped with 12 L-band antennas, and has an operational lifetime of 7 years.

launches.name: Soyuz STB/Fregat-MT | MetOp-C
launches.mission_desc: MetOp is a series of three polar orbiting meteorological satellites developed by the European Space Agency (ESA).

launches.name: Electron | It's Business Time (Rideshare)
launches.mission_desc: Electron's first commercial launch will feature two Lemur-2 cubesats for Spire Global, a single cubesat for GeoOptics, a NABEO drag sail demonstrator for High Performance Space Structure Systems, an IRVINE01 cubesat from the Irvine CubeSat STEM Program, and two Proxima cubesats from Fleet Space Technologies.
launches.location: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, Mahia Peninsula, New Zealand

launches.name: LVM-3 | GSAT-29
launches.mission_desc: GSAT-29 is a geostationary communications satellite developed by ISRO. GSAT-29 carries Ka x Ku multi-beam and optical communication payloads.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre Second Launch Pad

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Es'hail 2
launches.mission_desc: Es'hail 2 is a communications satellite operated by a Quatar based company. The satellite will operate at 26 degrees East longitude along a geostationary orbit to provide direct-to-home television services in the Middle East and North Africa region.

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Progress MS-10 (71P)
launches.mission_desc: The Progress resupply vehicle is an automated, unpiloted version of the Soyuz spacecraft that is used to bring supplies and fuel to the International Space Station.

launches.name: Antares 230 | Cygnus CRS NG-10 (S.S. John Young)
launches.mission_desc: This is the eleventh planned flight of the Orbital ATK's uncrewed resupply spacecraft Cygnus and its tenth flight to the International Space Station under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M17 & M18
launches.mission_desc: These two satellites will be used to provide global navigation coverage as part of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Long March 2D | Shiyan 6, Jiading-1 (OKW-1) & others
launches.mission_desc: Shiyan 6 is the main payload of the launch and is reported to be used for "space environment measurements and related technical tests". It was launched along with 4 small satellites, among which are a China's first privately designed low Earth orbit communications satellite Jiading-1 and China's first software-based satellite Tianzhi-1.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Vega | Mohammed VI-B
launches.mission_desc: A second Earth observation satellite for the Kingdom of Morocco. It was developed by Thales Alenia Space and Airbus. Satellite will be in particular used for mapping and land surveying activities, regional development, agricultural monitoring, the prevention and management of natural disasters, monitoring changes in the environment and desertification, as well as border and coastal surveillance.

launches.name: KSLV-2-TLV | Test Flight
launches.mission_desc: Suborbital test flight, reaching a maximum altitude of 209 km and a 151-second burn time

launches.name: PSLV-CA | HysIS
launches.mission_desc: HysIS (Hyperspectral Imaging Spectrometer) is a small Indian earth observation satellite developed by ISRO. The primary goal of HysIS is to study the earthâ€™s surface in visible, near infrared and shortwave infrared regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. It is launched along with 30 small satellites and cubesats for international companies.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Rokot / Briz-KM | 3 x Rodnik (Kosmos 2530, 2531, 2532)
launches.mission_desc: Rodnik is a series of military communications satellites.

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-11
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-11 begins expedition 58 by carrying Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Kononenko, CSA astronaut David Saint-Jacques and NASA astronaut Anne McClain to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Spaceflight SSO-A
launches.mission_desc: Dedicated rideshare launching payloads into sun-synchronous orbit. Payloads include ORS-6, EU:CROPIS, STPSat-5, BlackSky Global-1 to -4, HawkEye Pathfinder 1-3, Iceye, NEXTSat-1, 2 SkySats, Centauri II, and a Flock of Doves.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | GSAT-11 & GEO-KOMPSAT-2A
launches.mission_desc: GSAT-11 is an Indian geostationary communications satellite. It is based n the new I-6K Bus and carry 40 transponders in the Ku-band and Ka-band frequencies. GEO-KOMPSAT 2A is a South Korean geostationary meteorological satellite developed by KARI. The satellite will be used for weather and space weather observation.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | SpX CRS-16
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their 16th operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Long March 2D | SaudiSat 5A & 5B
launches.mission_desc: SaudiSat 5A and 5B are Earth observation satellites developed by KACST (King Abdulaziz City for Science & Technology). They share the launch with several microsatellites for private Chinese companies.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Long March 3B/E | Chang'e 4 (lander and rover)
launches.mission_desc: Chang'e 4 is a Chinese lunar exploration mission, incorporating a robotic lander and rover. Chang'e 4 will be China's second lunar lander and rover. The spacecraft is named after the Chinese Moon goddess. This will be the first mission to attempt soft landing on the far side of the Moon.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity VP-03
launches.mission_desc: Powered test flight of VSS Unity. Reached outer space for the first time according to the US definition of the space border.

launches.name: Electron | This One's For Pickering (VCLS ELaNa XIX)
launches.mission: This One's For Pickering (VCLS ELaNa XIX)
launches.mission_desc:
NASA's signed a Venture Class Launch Services contract with Rocket Lab to launch 10 cubesats as a part of CubeSat Launch Initiative Educational Launch of Nanosatellites (ELaNa) program.

Cubesats are:

ALBus / CeREs / CHOMPTT / Da Vinci / ISX / NMTSat / RSat-P / Shields 1 / STF 1 / CubeSail A / CubeSail B /TOMSat EagleScout / TOMSat R3 / SHFT 1
launches.location: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, Mahia Peninsula, New Zealand

launches.name: GSLV Mk II | GSAT-7A
launches.mission_desc: GSAT-7A is a geostationary communications satellite for the Indian Air Force (IAF).
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre Second Launch Pad

launches.name: Soyuz STA/Fregat | CSO-1
launches.mission_desc: The CSO-1 (Composante Spatiale Optique-1) satellite is the first of three new-generation high-resolution optical imaging satellites for the French military, replacing the Helios 2 spy satellite series.

launches.name: Proton-M/Briz-M | Blagovest N13L (Kosmos 2533)
launches.mission_desc: The third of four Blagovest communication satellites. It is a high throughput communications satellite used for high speed internet services, TV, radio broadcasting and voice/video networking.
launches.lsp: Khrunichev State Research and Production Space Center

launches.name: Long March 11 | Hongyun-1
launches.mission_desc: Hongyun is planned constellation of 156 low Earth orbit communications satellites by China Aerospace Science and Industry Corp (CASIC). Hongyun-1 is a technology demonstration satellite.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | GPS III SV01
launches.mission_desc:
GPS-IIIA (Global Positioning System) is the first evolution stage of the third generation of the GPS satellites. It consists of the first ten (known as "tranche") of GPS III satellites.

This program will improve position, navigation, and timing services for the warfighter and civil users worldwide and provide advanced anti-jam capabilities yielding superior system security, accuracy and reliability.

launches.name: Long March 3C | TJS-3 (TJSW-3)
launches.mission_desc: TJS 3 (Tongxin Jishu Shiyan) is a Chinese geostationary communications technology test satellite.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1a/Fregat-M | Kanopus-V No.5 & Kanopus-V No.6
launches.mission_desc: Kanopus-V is a series of Russian Earth observation satellites. They are used for real-time monitoring of natural and man-made emergencies, detecting forest fires, monitoring of land and water resources.

launches.name: Long March 2D/YZ-3 | Hongyan-1 & Yunhai-2 Group 01
launches.mission_desc:
Hongyan-1 is the first demonstration satellite for Hongyan, which is a planned constellation consisting of 320 satellites in low Earth orbit.

Yunhai-2 is a constellation of Chinese military meteorological satellites. Reportedly the satellites use Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Radio Occultation (GNSS-RO) to collect atmospheric data for weather prediction and for ionosphere, climate, and gravity research.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China
